title: Build an in-memory user service with validation and snapshots
prompt: Implement normalizeName, normalizeEmail, assertId in src/validation.js and createUserService in src/service.js, then re-export normalizeName, normalizeEmail, assertId, and createUserService from src/index.js. Use ES modules and only Node built-ins. normalizeName(name) requires a string, trims it, requires a length from 1 through 40 inclusive after trimming, and returns the trimmed value; interior spaces are preserved. normalizeEmail(email) requires a string, trims and lowercases it, and requires it to match /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/u, returning the normalized value. assertId(id) requires a positive safe integer and returns it. Each validator throws an Error for invalid input. createUserService() returns { create, get, findByEmail, update, remove, list }. create({ name, email }) reads only those fields, validates them, rejects an email already in use case-insensitively, and returns a fresh { id, name, email } object. IDs start at 1 and increase after each successful create; failed creates do not consume an ID. get(id) returns a fresh user or null for an unknown valid ID; findByEmail(email) normalizes the email and returns a fresh user or null. update(id, changes) throws for an unknown ID; changes must be an object whose only allowed keys are name and/or email, with anything else throwing. Validate all new values and reject duplicate emails before changing state, then return a fresh updated user. remove(id) returns true when a user was deleted, false for an unknown valid ID. list() returns a new array of fresh user objects sorted by ascending id. Every returned user must be a snapshot: mutating it must not affect stored state.
